metadata.title: The RBM mutual-information lower bound is fixed by the marginals, not by a learning principle

creators.name: Monteverde, Vicente Humberto
creators.affiliation: Universidad del Museo Social Argentino (UMSA), Argentina

metadata.description: A recent review (Sec. 3.2 and Fig. 4 there, after Ref. [34] of the review) characterizes a restricted Boltzmann machine (RBM) learner by two numbers for each visible–hidden pair. The first is the covariance η=Cov(σ_z^v,σ_z^h), which is read from the imaginary part of an out-of-time-order correlator. The second is the mutual information I. The pair (I,η) is shown to lie between analytic bounds LB(η) and UB(η). Trained RBMs sit on the lower bound for every system size and field ratio of transverse-field Ising drivers, and the review reads this as a learning principle: the network would use the least mutual information compatible with the covariance. We point out that a pair of ±1 units is fixed by three numbers, the two marginals m_v=⟨σ_z^v⟩, m_h=⟨σ_z^h⟩ and η. In those variables, LB(η) is exactly the case m_v=m_h=0, and it is the minimum of I over the marginals at fixed η. UB(η) is the perfectly correlated pair with |m_v|=|m_h|=√(1-|η|). The transverse-field Ising driver is ℤ_2-symmetric, so a symmetric RBM has zero marginals and sits on LB by construction. We test the consequence that could have failed. With exact enumeration (n=6 visible spins, α=1), a longitudinal field of 0.1–0.3 moves the same learner off LB by up to 0.17 bits, in step with the measured marginals. In the ordered phase, a symmetry-broken and a symmetric RBM of the same target sit off and on LB respectively. The OTOC reading of η is unaffected; we suggest reporting the marginals alongside (I,η).
metadata.notes: Every numerical claim is reproduced by the open-source library qang (pip install qang, version 0.6.14) and pinned by its tests; predictions were committed before each run.
